subtitulo: Patterns, not just words: writing about AI
descripcion: At C2 the discipline extends past single overused words to overused sentence patterns and rhetorical moves — recognising when a favourite structure of your own has become a tic, not just avoiding very and good, and varying structure deliberately across a longer piece.

ejemplos.texto: The report was thorough, if occasionally repetitive.
For once, I'll skip the caveat: this is a mistake.

notas: A rhetorical tic — always softening before disagreeing, always hedging before a claim — is a higher-order overused pattern that word-level precision alone won't fix.
Deliberately breaking your own habitual pattern once in a longer piece (for once, I'll skip the caveat) reads as self-aware rather than inconsistent.
Varying sentence openings across a paragraph is a mechanical discipline worth checking for in any longer piece.

es.en: Spanish speakers have usually learned to avoid very and good by this level, so the remaining gap is structural: a favourite Spanish sentence pattern, such as a fronted subordinate clause, can become a personal tic in English without the writer noticing.
es.es: A este nivel, los hispanohablantes normalmente ya han aprendido a evitar abusar de «very» y «good», por lo que la brecha restante es estructural: un patrón de oración favorito del español, por ejemplo una subordinada adelantada, puede convertirse en un tic personal en inglés sin que el escritor lo note.

de.en: A typical German tic is the overuse of actually, carried over from «eigentlich», and sentence-initial so, carried over from «also». Both are harmless once, but noticeable when repeated.
de.de: Ein typischer deutscher Tick ist die übermäßige Verwendung von «actually», beeinflusst durch «eigentlich», und von satzinitialem «so», beeinflusst durch «also». Einzeln sind beide harmlos, bei Wiederholung fallen sie jedoch auf.

it.en: A typical Italian tic is basically or let's say, carried over from «praticamente» and «diciamo». Both are harmless once, but noticeable when repeated.
it.it: Un tipico tic italiano è l'uso ripetuto di «basically» o «let's say», influenzato da «praticamente» e «diciamo». Una volta sono innocui, ma se ripetuti diventano evidenti.

fr.en: A typical French tic is in fact or actually, carried over from «en fait». It is harmless once, but noticeable when repeated in polished English.
fr.fr: Un tic français typique est l'emploi répété de «in fact» ou «actually», calqué sur «en fait». Une fois, cela ne gêne pas ; répété, cela devient visible dans un anglais soigné.

pt.en: A typical Portuguese tic is basically or like, carried over from «basicamente» and, in Brazil, «tipo». Both are harmless once, but noticeable when repeated.
pt.pt: Um tic típico de falantes de português é usar demais «basically» ou «like», influenciado por «basicamente» e, no Brasil, «tipo». Uma vez, ambos são inofensivos; repetidos, chamam atenção.

errores: Fixing word-level overuse while leaving structural or rhetorical tics untouched.
Repeating the same sentence opener across several consecutive sentences.
Always applying the same rhetorical softening move regardless of whether it fits the point.

es: Opening sentence after sentence with «*Hay que decir que*» → *It must be said that*.
de: Opening sentences with «*Es ist so, dass*» → *It is so that*, which is not idiomatic English at all.
it: Opening sentence after sentence with «*Diciamo che*» → *Let's say that*.
fr: Opening sentence after sentence with «*Il faut dire que*» → *It must be said that*.
pt: Opening sentences with «*É de referir que*» → *It is to refer that* instead of *It is worth noting that*.

mision.consigna: Write a paragraph on whether AI will supplant or augment professionals — then cut every rhetorical move you use by default.
requisitos: name two of your habitual moves (e.g. rhetorical question, triplet)
use *to supplant*, *to augment human capabilities* and *obsolete*

microtareas.texto: Underline your habitual moves in something you wrote about *algorithmic bias*.
Record 2 minutes on *accountability*; listen for spoken tics.

autochequeo: Have I checked for repeated sentence openers across a paragraph?
Have I noticed and varied my own habitual rhetorical moves at least once?
Is every very + adjective replaced with a precise word?
Does at least one sentence deliberately break my usual pattern?
Would a careful reader notice repetition of structure, not just of words?
promptCorreccion: Focus only on lexical and structural precision. Check for repeated sentence openers and habitual rhetorical moves, not just overused words. Do not rewrite the text.
